question: The photograph in the Whitney Museum of American Art's collection with accession number 2022.128 shows a person holding a book. Which military unit did the author of this book join in 1813? Answer without using articles.

history.name: user
history.content: The photograph in the Whitney Museum of American Art's collection with accession number 2022.128 shows a person holding a book. Which military unit did the author of this book join in 1813? Answer without using articles.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Task: Identify the Whitney object 2022.128, determine the book visible, identify the book's author, then find which military unit that author joined in 1813. Plan: 1) Locate 2022.128 in Whitney's online collection or open-access dataset. 2) Extract the book title/author from the object record. 3) Research the author's biography focusing on 1813. 4) Cross-verify with at least two sources. 5) Answer with no articles.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, first try locating the object entry via Whitney's site search or the open-access data. Search for Whitney 2022.128 and see if the collection or open-access dataset references it.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: I searched for site:whitney.org "2022.128" and variants like "Whitney accession 2022.128". The direct collection page did not surface immediately. I see the Whitney Open Access page referencing nightly-updated CSVs and a GitHub repository where artworks.csv and artists.csv can be downloaded. This should contain an accession number field we can query.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open the Whitney Museum Open Access GitHub repository and navigate to the artworks.csv file so we can search for accession number 2022.128.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened GitHub repo whitneymuseum/open-access. I see artworks.csv and artists.csv. I'll open artworks.csv and access the raw view to search for accession number 2022.128.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open the raw artworks.csv and search within it for "2022.128". Report the matching row with title, artist, date, medium, and any descriptive fields mentioning the book.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: I opened the raw artworks.csv and searched for "2022.128". Found a row with fields including accession_number: 2022.128; classification: Photograph; artist: Irina Rozovsky; title: Student with Ivan Vyzhigin; date: 2012; medium: inkjet print; dimensions listed; credit line Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, 2022.128. The description field notes: "A young man seated, holding a paperback copy of Ivan Vyzhigin by Faddey Bulgarin; the cover in Cyrillic is partially visible."

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Great. Confirm the book author and pull any additional context from the description. Then we will research the author's 1813 military affiliation.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: From the artworks.csv row: book_title appears as "Ivan Vyzhigin"; book_author listed explicitly as "Faddey Bulgarin (Tadeusz Bułharyn)" in a note field; description reiterates that the sitter holds a copy of Bulgarin’s novel. So the author is Faddey Bulgarin.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Now research Faddey Bulgarin’s biography focusing on the year 1813. Identify the unit he joined in 1813. Please find a reliable source.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: I checked Faddey Bulgarin’s biography on a reputable encyclopedia and Wikipedia. Both note that in 1813, Bulgarin joined the Russian–German Legion under General Wallmoden to fight against Napoleon. One phrasing: "In 1813 he entered the Russian–German Legion."

history.name: Assistant
history.content: So, based on the object record, the book author is Faddey Bulgarin, and sources state that in 1813 he joined Russian–German Legion. I will cross-check to avoid confusing this with King's German Legion, which is a different formation.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Good idea. WebSurfer, provide a second independent confirmation that Bulgarin joined Russian–German Legion in 1813.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Found a Russian-language biographical reference and a scholarly summary that both confirm: in 1813 Bulgarin served in the Russian–German Legion (Русско-немецкий легион). Another English-language overview mentions his service with Wallmoden’s forces in the Russian–German Legion during the campaigns of 1813–1814.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Clarification: Russian–German Legion (1813) was a formation in Russian service composed largely of German deserters and prisoners-of-war, later incorporated into Prussian service. King's German Legion was a British Army unit (1803–1816). The correct 1813 unit for Bulgarin is Russian–German Legion, not King's German Legion.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Summary so far: Whitney 2022.128 is a photograph of a person holding Ivan Vyzhigin by Faddey Bulgarin. Multiple sources confirm Bulgarin joined Russian–German Legion in 1813. We must answer with no articles. Prepare to provide the unit name exactly as requested.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: Local note compiled: artworks.csv entry for accession 2022.128 includes: book_title: Ivan Vyzhigin; book_author: Faddey Bulgarin; description explicitly references Bulgarin’s novel. This aligns with the external biographical finding.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: All checks complete. Assistant, respond with the unit name exactly, no articles. Use: Russian-German Legion.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Acknowledged. Based on the sources and confirmation, I will answer with: Russian-German Legion.

history.name: Assistant

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Submitting answer.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: If needed later, I can provide the URLs of the biographical sources that state Bulgarin joined the Russian–German Legion in 1813.

mistake_reason: Reasoning-Action Mismatch (FM-2.6): Prior steps established that the book is by Faddey Bulgarin and multiple sources explicitly confirm he joined Russian-German Legion in 1813. The orchestrator instructed the Assistant to answer exactly "Russian-German Legion," and the Assistant even acknowledged this plan at step 19. However, at step 20 the Assistant executed a contradictory action by outputting "King's German Legion," a different unit, directly contradicting the stated reasoning and plan. This inter-agent misalignment between the logical conclusion and the final action caused the failure.
